top_story: Across the occupied West Bank, the Hebron shooting on 23 October triggered a rapid Israeli escalation from mosque closures and intensified raids to a broader punitive campaign centered on demolitions and threatened displacement, while ministers used the attack to renew calls to dismantle the Palestinian Authority. The pressure on Palestinians is not confined to movement restrictions and armed incursions, as evidence of electroshock abuse against detainees points to coercion extending through arrest and custody with continued foreign-enabled supply. In Sudan, one year after the UAE-backed RSF seized El-Fasher, Amnesty’s estimate that only seven percent of the city’s former peak population remains shows how sustained violence, torture, and disappearances have hollowed out urban life and driven mass civilian flight. The regional pattern is one in which armed actors and their external backers are deepening control through collective punishment and abuse, with civilian communities bearing the strategic cost.
